title: OpenGL foundations
description: Window, shaders and an indexed square.
goal: Trace four vertices and six indices, then inspect how two triangles form a square.
note: Original sets a blue clear color and uses legacy shader inputs; graphics execution has not been verified here. Fragment color components exceed 1 and renderColorLocation is never looked up. The browser visual is a new teaching reconstruction.

title: Board input and validation
goal: Place P markers, reject occupied cells and fill the board. This stage does not yet implement a two-player game.
note: Original recognizes q, parses row/column strings, rejects invalid and occupied cells, and prints a board. The mock uses clickable cells instead of Scanner input.

title: Separating input and board logic
description: Reusable I/O and scripted board tests.
goal: Replay the original testPlay sequence, including a repeated occupied cell, then reset.
note: The current folder, old folder and nested ZIP contain variants. getBoard() clones only the outer array. The mock uses independent state copies and labels that safety difference.

title: A machine opponent
description: Threat detection, wins and random fallback.
goal: Play against the source-inspired block-first machine and inspect its decision after every move.
note: The archived machine blocks P before checking its own X win, then chooses randomly. The browser follows that priority with a repeatable seeded fallback and stops safely at terminal states; it is not minimax or Java Random replay.

title: Singleton window manager
description: One shared window across repeated get calls.
goal: Call get() and get(width,height,x,y), compare object identity and change a modeled window.
note: The original A5 setter changes stored dimensions but does not call glfwSetWindowSize, so reported and actual window size may differ. The mock displays both rather than silently claiming native resizing.

title: Reusable tile renderer
description: A grid becomes vertex and index buffers.
goal: Adjust rows, columns, size, padding and offset; inspect one tile and its triangles.
note: Original derives row/column counts from the window rather than using the render arguments. It allocates GPU buffers every frame despite a comment saying only once. The mock is a corrected bounded geometry explorer with top-left SVG coordinates, not OpenGL.

title: Ping-pong arrays
description: Read live, write next, then swap.
goal: Write a cell, shuffle, calculate toroidal neighbor sums and explicitly promote the next buffer.
note: Source loadFile reads file dimensions but uses constructor dimensions; randomizeInRange fills next then calls a shuffle that copies live over it. The mock parser honors file dimensions and its labeled range operation is corrected.

title: Binary arrays and unit-level tests
description: Exact populations, degree-two neighbors and fixtures.
goal: Explore a binary board, compare both neighborhood definitions and run new deterministic checks.
note: Archived test driver has four ult methods; ult_a constructs 5×5 arrays for 7×7 files. Degree-two offsets are distance-two axial plus diagonal cells. New tests below are portfolio tests, not claimed archived Java test results.

title: Conway’s Game of Life
description: The final project combines data and rendering.
goal: Run a toroidal simulation, edit cells, load the archived 16×16 pattern, and inspect live/next generations.
note: Final source separates GoLArray, WindowManager, Renderer and GeometryManager. Java driver defaults to 100×100 with 20% live cells; the browser opens a smaller editable blinker and offers 100×100 mode. The 12-method archived test driver includes graphics boot and partly randomized setups, so it is not proof of a deterministic passing suite.
